Returns IServiceCollection The service collection. Examples using DynamicQueryBuilder; using DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enums.Helpers.Databases; using DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Helpers; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); var settings = new DynamicQueryBuilderSettings( builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DynamicQueryBuilder") ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Connection string 'DynamicQueryBuilder' is missing."), DatabaseDriver.POSTGRESQL); builder.Services.AddDynamicQueryBuilder(settings); Remarks Registers two scoped services: IGetDatabaseMetaData, created with settings, and IQueryBuilderSetup, implemented by QueryBuilder. Known issue: QueryBuilder keeps the clauses of the query being built, and the scoped registration gives every consumer in the same scope (for example, the same HTTP request) the same instance, so their clauses are mixed.

docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces..summary: Interface IQueryBuilder Namespace DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces.Builders Assembly DynamicQueryBuilder.dll Defines a builder for constructing SQL queries. public interface IQueryBuilder Remarks Column names, joined tables, join conditions, operator strings and values are inserted into the generated SQL verbatim, and so is the table of FromTable(string), except that it is converted to upper case. Nothing is parameterized, quoted or escaped, and nothing is checked against the metadata given to Setup(Dictionary<string, List<string>>) except the table set by FromTable(string). Do not pass untrusted input to these methods: it allows SQL injection. String literals must carry their own quotes, for example "'Alice'". Filters are emitted in the order they were added, joined by AND or OR without parentheses, so the database's operator precedence applies. The AND or OR of the first filter is not emitted. Each clause method changes this instance and returns it. Columns, joins, filters, GROUP BY and ORDER BY items are only appended, and there is no way to remove them or reset the builder; FromTable(string) and SetLimit(int) replace their value. The generate methods do not change the instance. Methods Columns(params string[]) Specifies the columns to select in the query. When no column is specified, SELECT * is generated. It does not stop the query methods from being called before Setup(Dictionary<string, List<string>>): QueryBuilder also implements IQueryBuilder publicly, and only the two generate methods check that setup happened. Only the keys are used: the table given to FromTable(string), converted to upper case, must be one of them, compared with the dictionary's own key comparer (case-sensitive by default). The column lists are stored but never read, so columns are not validated. Returns IQueryBuilder The same builder instance, as an IQueryBuilder that provides the full set of query-building methods.

docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces..title: Interface IGetDatabaseMetaData | DynamicQueryBuilder
docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces..summary: Interface IGetDatabaseMetaData Namespace DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces.Helpers Assembly DynamicQueryBuilder.dll Interface for getting database metadata. public interface IGetDatabaseMetaData Methods GetDatabaseTablesMetaDataAsync() Get the metadata of the database tables. Task<Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, List<DatabaseTablesMetaData>>>> GetDatabaseTablesMetaDataAsync() Returns Task<Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, List<DatabaseTablesMetaData>>>> A dictionary keyed by schema name. Each value is keyed by table name and holds one DatabaseTablesMetaData per row of the catalog query. Remarks Each call opens a connection with the configured settings and runs the catalog query of GetMetadataQuery(DatabaseDriver); nothing is cached. The schemas pg_catalog and information_schema (PostgreSQL) or mysql, information_schema and performance_schema (MySQL) are excluded. Names are returned as the database reports them. This schema, table and columns shape is not the table-to-column-names dictionary that Setup(Dictionary<string, List<string>>) expects. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when unable to create a command. ArgumentException Thrown when the connection string is null, empty or whitespace, or by the driver when it is malformed. NotSupportedException Thrown when the configured driver is not supported. DbException Thrown, as the driver's subtype (NpgsqlException or MySqlException), when connecting or running the catalog query fails. With MYSQL the query currently always fails with a MySqlException.

docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enum.summary: Enum DatabaseDriver Namespace DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enums.Helpers.Databases Assembly DynamicQueryBuilder.dll Database drivers for reading table metadata. public enum DatabaseDriver Fields MYSQL = 1 MySQL driver (MySql.Data). Known issue: reading metadata with this driver fails. The MySQL catalog query selects TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME and COLUMN_NAME without a table qualifier although both joined views have these columns, so MySQL rejects it with a MySqlException ("Column 'TABLE_SCHEMA' in field list is ambiguous"). POSTGRESQL = 0 PostgreSQL driver (Npgsql). Remarks The driver selects the connection type and the catalog query used to read metadata. It does not affect the SQL produced by the query builder.

docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enum.title: Enum JoinOperators | DynamicQueryBuilder
docs/api/DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enum.summary: Enum JoinOperators Namespace DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enums.SqlOperators Assembly DynamicQueryBuilder.dll Represents SQL join operators. public enum JoinOperators Fields CROSS_JOIN = 4 CROSS JOIN - Intended to produce a Cartesian product of the tables. Known issue: the builder always emits it with an ON clause, which standard SQL does not allow for a cross join, so the generated SQL is not a plain cross join. FULL_JOIN = 3 FULL JOIN (or FULL OUTER JOIN) - Returns all records from both tables, with matching records when available. MySQL has no FULL JOIN: it reads the emitted text as an alias (FULL) plus a plain join, or fails. INNER_JOIN = 0 INNER JOIN - Returns only records that have matching entries in both tables LEFT_JOIN = 1 LEFT JOIN (or LEFT OUTER JOIN) - Returns all records from the left table and the matching records from the right table RIGHT_JOIN = 2 RIGHT JOIN (or RIGHT OUTER JOIN) - Returns all records from the right table and the matching records from the left table SELF_JOIN = 5 SELF JOIN - Intended to join a table with itself. Known issue: the builder emits the text SELF JOIN, which is not an SQL join type. PostgreSQL and MySQL read SELF as an alias for the FROM table, so the query fails when the condition names the FROM table and otherwise runs as a plain inner join.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | DynamicQueryBuilder
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Warning Pre-alpha: don't use it in production. Not on NuGet. The library isn't published. The DynamicQueryBuilder package on nuget.org is an unrelated project. The API will change. A rewrite is planned, and nothing here is stable. No protection against SQL injection. Values, identifiers (table and column names), join conditions and operators are concatenated into the SQL text, with no parameters and no escaping. Never pass untrusted input. See the security policy. Almost no validation. The only check on names is that the upper-cased FROM table is a key of the map passed to Setup. The column lists in that map are never read, and columns, joined tables, conditions and values aren't checked. 📦 Installation DynamicQueryBuilder is not published on NuGet yet. The DynamicQueryBuilder package on nuget.org belongs to an unrelated project, so don't install it expecting this library. To try it, clone the repository and add a project reference to src/DynamicQueryBuilder/DynamicQueryBuilder.csproj. The library targets net8.0 and net9.0. From the folder that contains both the clone and your project: git clone https://github.com/gabriel-sisjr/DynamicQueryBuilder.git dotnet add YourApp/YourApp.csproj reference DynamicQueryBuilder/src/DynamicQueryBuilder/DynamicQueryBuilder.csproj Or add the reference to your project file yourself: <ItemGroup> <ProjectReference Include="../DynamicQueryBuilder/src/DynamicQueryBuilder/DynamicQueryBuilder.csproj" /> </ItemGroup> 🛠 Usage Setting Up DynamicQueryBuilder Register the services in Program.cs. AddDynamicQueryBuilder takes a DynamicQueryBuilderSettings with the connection string and the database driver: using DynamicQueryBuilder; using DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enums.Helpers.Databases; using DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Helpers; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); var connectionString = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DynamicQueryBuilder") ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Connection string 'DynamicQueryBuilder' is not set."); builder.Services.AddDynamicQueryBuilder( new DynamicQueryBuilderSettings(connectionString, DatabaseDriver.POSTGRESQL)); This registers two scoped services: the metadata reader (IGetDatabaseMetaData) and a query builder (IQueryBuilderSetup). IQueryBuilder itself isn't registered. Inject the metadata reader where you need it. GetDatabaseTablesMetaDataAsync takes no arguments; the driver comes from the settings: using DynamicQueryBuilder.Interfaces.Helpers; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] public class YourController : ControllerBase { private readonly IGetDatabaseMetaData _getDatabaseMetaData; public YourController(IGetDatabaseMetaData getDatabaseMetaData) { _getDatabaseMetaData = getDatabaseMetaData; } /* * This method will return your schema tables metadata. */ [HttpGet] public async Task<IActionResult> GetDatabaseMetadata() { var metadata = await _getDatabaseMetaData.GetDatabaseTablesMetaDataAsync(); return Ok(metadata); } } The result describes your database schema, so don't expose it without authentication. Method Response The method returns a dictionary of schema name → table name → a list of column entries, with names in the database's own casing. Each entry has: Column name (column) Data type (columnType) primaryKey, which despite its name doesn't tell you whether the column is part of the primary key. This is a known defect. On PostgreSQL it holds the column's default expression (column_default), or null when the column has no default. In the example below, users.id is a serial primary key and shows its nextval(...) default, orders.id is an identity primary key and shows null, and orders.total_amount isn't a key but shows its default, 0. On MySQL the field is meant to hold COLUMN_KEY (PRI, UNI, MUL or empty), but the MySQL catalog query currently fails before returning anything, with Column 'TABLE_SCHEMA' in field list is ambiguous. Foreign-key target (relatedSchema, relatedTable, relatedColumn), or null when the column isn't a foreign key or the connecting role doesn't own the tables. PostgreSQL shows foreign-key targets only to the tables' owner, even if another role has every table privilege. Usually there's one entry per column. Columns in a composite foreign key, or in more than one foreign key, get one entry per target column, including wrong pairings: with a two-column key, each column is paired with both target columns. The rows aren't sorted, so the column order isn't predictable: it can differ between two databases with the same tables. Example of Returned Structure The reader's result for a PostgreSQL database with these two tables, as JSON: CREATE TABLE users ( id serial PRIMARY KEY, name varchar(100) NOT NULL, email text UNIQUE ); CREATE TABLE orders ( id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id), total_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 ); { "public": { "orders": [ { "column": "id", "columnType": "bigint", "primaryKey": null, "relatedSchema": null, "relatedTable": null, "relatedColumn": null }, { "column": "user_id", "columnType": "integer", "primaryKey": null, "relatedSchema": "public", "relatedTable": "users", "relatedColumn": "id" }, { "column": "total_amount", "columnType": "numeric", "primaryKey": "0", "relatedSchema": null, "relatedTable": null, "relatedColumn": null } ], "users": [ { "column": "id", "columnType": "integer", "primaryKey": "nextval('users_id_seq'::regclass)", "relatedSchema": null, "relatedTable": null, "relatedColumn": null }, { "column": "email", "columnType": "text", "primaryKey": null, "relatedSchema": null, "relatedTable": null, "relatedColumn": null }, { "column": "name", "columnType": "character varying", "primaryKey": null, "relatedSchema": null, "relatedTable": null, "relatedColumn": null } ] } } This isn't the shape Setup takes (upper-case table name → column names), so you build the Setup map yourself. Building Queries You get a builder from QueryBuilder.Create(), from new QueryBuilder(), or as IQueryBuilderSetup from dependency injection. Either way, call Setup first: it takes a map of table names to column names. GenerateSql and GenerateFormattedSql throw InvalidOperationException if Setup wasn't called or if the FROM table isn't a key of the map. That's the only check: the column lists are never read. FromTable upper-cases the table name before that lookup, so the keys must be upper-case. With ["Users"] instead of ["USERS"], GenerateSql throws Undefined or Invalid table. A dictionary created with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase accepts either. The samples below use QueryBuilder.Create() and this map: using DynamicQueryBuilder.Builders; using DynamicQueryBuilder.Models.Enums.SqlOperators; var tables = new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["USERS"] = ["Id", "Name", "Email", "Age"], ["ORDERS"] = ["Id", "UserId", "TotalAmount"] }; The builder is mutable. Columns, Join, the filters, GroupBy and OrderBy add to what's already there, while FromTable, SetLimit and Setup replace their value, so a reused builder carries parts of the previous query into the next one. The IQueryBuilderSetup from dependency injection is one instance per scope, so everything that resolves it while handling the same request shares it, filters included. When you need isolation, use QueryBuilder.Create() for each query. Basic SELECT Query var sql = QueryBuilder.Create() .Setup(tables) .FromTable("Users") .Columns("Id", "Name", "Email") .GenerateSql(); // Output: SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM USERS Adding WHERE Filters var sql = QueryBuilder.Create() .Setup(tables) .FromTable("Users") .Columns("Id", "Name") .FilterBy("Age", ComparisonOperators.GREATER_THAN, "18") .GenerateSql(); // Output: SELECT Id, Name FROM USERS WHERE Age > 18 The value is copied into the SQL as written. To compare with a string, pass the quotes yourself ("'Alice'"); nothing is escaped. Using JOINs var sql = QueryBuilder.Create() .Setup(tables) .FromTable("Users") .Columns("Users.Id", "Users.Name", "Orders.TotalAmount") .Join(JoinOperators.INNER_JOIN, "Orders", "Users.Id = Orders.UserId") .GenerateSql(); // Output: SELECT Users.Id, Users.Name, Orders.TotalAmount FROM USERS INNER JOIN Orders ON Users.Id = Orders.UserId Only FROM is checked against the map: the joined table, the column names and the condition are copied as written.

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | DynamicQueryBuilder
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction DynamicQueryBuilder is a pre-alpha .NET library that builds SQL SELECT statements with a fluent API and reads table and column metadata from a database (PostgreSQL works; MySQL currently fails). It isn't published on NuGet, its API will change, and it concatenates every value and identifier into the SQL text, so never pass it untrusted input. To try it, see Getting Started.

index.html.title: DynamicQueryBuilder | DynamicQueryBuilder
index.html.summary: DynamicQueryBuilder A .NET library for building SQL SELECT statements with a fluent API, plus a reader that lists the tables and columns of a database. Warning Pre-alpha: don't use it in production. Not on NuGet. The library isn't published. The DynamicQueryBuilder package on nuget.org is an unrelated project. The API will change. A rewrite is planned, and nothing here is stable. No protection against SQL injection. Values, identifiers (table and column names), join conditions and operators are concatenated into the SQL text, with no parameters and no escaping. Never pass untrusted input. See the security policy. Almost no validation. The only check on names is that the upper-cased FROM table is a key of the map passed to Setup. The column lists in that map are never read, and columns, joined tables, conditions and values aren't checked. 🚀 Features Core Features Fluent API that builds one SQL SELECT statement and returns it as a string Registration with dependency injection through AddDynamicQueryBuilder Database Support The metadata reader connects to PostgreSQL (Npgsql) or MySQL (MySql.Data). It works with PostgreSQL; with MySQL it currently fails (see Known limitations below). The query builder doesn't depend on the database: it emits the same SQL for both. Query Capabilities SELECT, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses Filters joined with AND (FilterBy) or OR (OrFilterBy) Generates both formatted and unformatted SQL queries SQL Operators Comparison operators (=, <>, >, <, >=, <=) Logical operators (AND, OR) String operators (LIKE, ILIKE) Range operators (BETWEEN, NOT BETWEEN) Inclusion operators (IN, NOT IN) Null operators (IS NULL, IS NOT NULL) Any other operator, passed as free text Additional Features Database metadata reader: the columns of every table the database user can access, grouped by schema and table, with each column's data type and foreign-key target (see Known limitations) Known limitations Filters are joined in call order, without parentheses: a AND b OR c is evaluated as (a AND b) OR c. The builder ignores the database driver, which only the metadata reader uses. It emits ILIKE and FULL JOIN for MySQL too, but MySQL has neither: ILIKE is a syntax error, and FULL is read as an alias for the FROM table, so the join either fails or runs as a plain join. FromTable upper-cases the table name using the current culture and emits it unquoted. PostgreSQL folds it back to lower case, so FROM USERS finds users but not a table created as "Users". MySQL on Linux compares table names case-sensitively by default, so FROM USERS doesn't find users. There's no dedicated support for schema.table or aliases: free text such as FromTable("public.users") works only if the Setup map has the upper-cased string ("PUBLIC.USERS") as a key. JoinOperators.CROSS_JOIN always adds an ON clause, which PostgreSQL rejects. JoinOperators.SELF_JOIN emits SELF JOIN, which isn't a join type: the database reads SELF as an alias for the FROM table, so the join fails if the condition names that table and otherwise runs as a plain join. FilterBy and OrFilterBy accept StringOperators.CONCAT but always throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for it. SetOperators, ArithmeticOperators and LogicalOperators.NOT exist, but no builder method uses them. With MySQL the metadata reader fails: its catalog query throws Column 'TABLE_SCHEMA' in field list is ambiguous. Despite its name, the reader's PrimaryKey field doesn't tell you whether a column is part of the primary key. On PostgreSQL it holds the column's default expression. On PostgreSQL the foreign-key fields are null unless the connecting role owns the tables, even if it has every table privilege: information_schema.constraint_column_usage only shows tables owned by a currently enabled role. Columns in a composite foreign key, or in more than one foreign key, come back once per target column, including wrong pairings: with a two-column key, each column is paired with both target columns. The reader returns schema → table → columns, in the database's own casing. That isn't the shape Setup takes, so you build the Setup map yourself. 📚 Documentation Getting started shows how to try the library from a clone of the repository, register it and build queries. The API reference is generated from the source code. 💡 Examples The repository's examples folder has two projects. Both are part of DynamicQueryBuilder.sln and reference the library project directly. See examples/README.md for how to run them. ClientWebAPI: an ASP.NET Core API that returns the metadata reader's output over HTTP. It has no authentication, so run it locally only. It needs a PostgreSQL connection string under ConnectionStrings:DynamicQueryBuilder: run dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:DynamicQueryBuilder" "<value>" in examples/ClientWebAPI/ClientWebAPI, or set the ConnectionStrings__DynamicQueryBuilder environment variable. Without it, the app stops at startup. ConsoleClient: a placeholder that prints "Hello, World!". It doesn't use the library yet. ✅ Roadmap A rewrite of the core is planned before the first release. It covers: [ ] A core that only generates SQL and its parameters: values sent as parameters, never as text [ ] Quoted identifiers, schema.table and aliases [ ] Grouped conditions: AND, OR and NOT with parentheses [ ] SQL generated for each database, starting with PostgreSQL and MySQL [ ] Every table and column checked against the schema read from the database [ ] Working metadata readers: real primary keys, composite foreign keys and a MySQL query that runs [ ] Tests that run the generated SQL against real databases [ ] More documentation and complete examples [ ] A first pre-release on NuGet, under a different package ID [ ] SQL Server support before 1.0 [ ] Target frameworks net10.0 and net8.0, plus netstandard2.0 for the core 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request.
